note: One contextual image per curated highlight. Museum displays, reconstructions and artefacts are explicitly distinguished from originals and underwater excavation photographs. The English Wikipedia lead image Nemi Ship Hull 1930.jpg was rejected: its file page reports PD-Italy with unconfirmed US status. The Commons 1929 photograph Nemi-Schiff.jpg is used instead.

images.caption: The original Oseberg ship on display in Oslo, photographed in 2016.
images.alt: The Oseberg ship's surviving wooden hull and tall curved prow on display inside a museum.

images.caption: The original Gokstad ship in its museum display—not the burial site.

images.caption: Surviving timbers of the Tune ship displayed in Oslo.

images.alt: The surviving wooden remains of Skuldelev 1 supported in the Viking Ship Museum.

images.caption: A Viking longship model at Hedeby—not a photograph of the original hull.
images.alt: A museum model of a Viking longship at Hedeby, showing its reconstructed hull and rigging.

images.caption: The surviving Kyrenia hull in its museum display.
images.alt: Surviving timbers of the ancient Kyrenia ship arranged in their hull shape indoors.

images.caption: The Antikythera recovery expedition aboard Mykali, winter 1900–1901—not an underwater view of the wreck.
images.alt: A historical group photograph of divers, crew and officials on the deck of a ship during the Antikythera recovery expedition.

images.caption: A reconstruction model of the Mahdia ship at the Bardo Museum—not the surviving original hull.
images.alt: A museum reconstruction of the Mahdia merchant ship with its hull, mast and rigging.

images.caption: A reconstruction of the Madrague de Giens merchant ship in Mainz—not the excavated wreck itself.
images.alt: A museum reconstruction model of the Roman merchant ship from Madrague de Giens.

images.caption: Inscribed ivory tusks from the Bajo de la Campana cargo—not a surviving ship hull.
images.alt: Ancient ivory tusks with Phoenician inscriptions from the Bajo de la Campana wreck displayed in a museum.

images.caption: A wooden model of the Uluburun ship—not the original Bronze Age hull.
images.alt: A wooden museum model reconstructing the hull and rigging of the Uluburun ship.

images.caption: A recovered Nemi hull in 1929, before the ships were destroyed by fire in 1944. Published in Bilderwoche.
images.alt: A historical photograph of a large Nemi ship hull exposed during recovery from Lake Nemi in 1929.

images.caption: The recovered Vasa viewed from the bow in its museum—not the original sinking location.
images.alt: The towering bow and preserved wooden hull of Vasa displayed inside its museum.

images.caption: The surviving Mary Rose hull undergoing polyethylene-glycol conservation in Portsmouth.
images.alt: The surviving half-hull of Mary Rose supported inside a conservation building.

images.caption: Jacob Hägg's later depiction of Kronan—not a contemporary photograph or an underwater wreck survey.
